questions.q: What is the defining restriction on a Q# `function`?
options: It must return a `Result` type
It is pure and deterministic and can never touch a qubit, use randomness, or call an `operation`
It can only be called from inside a `use` block
It must take exactly one `Qubit` parameter
questions.explain: A function in Q# is a pure, deterministic classical computation. It cannot touch qubits, cannot use quantum randomness, and the compiler forbids it from calling an operation.

questions.q: In the call graph between operations and functions, which direction is allowed?
options: Operations may call functions, but functions may never call operations
Functions may call operations, but operations may never call functions
Neither can ever call the other
Both can call each other freely
questions.explain: Dependency only flows one direction: operations may freely call functions (pure classical logic is always safe to use from quantum code), but a function calling an operation is a compile-time error.

questions.q: Why does the Q# compiler reject a function that calls the intrinsic operation `H`?
options: Because `H` is deprecated in modern QDK syntax
Because `H` requires an array argument, not a single qubit
Because `H` is an `operation`, and a `function` is not permitted to call an `operation` under any circumstances
Because `H` can only be called from within Python, not Q#
questions.explain: H is declared as an intrinsic operation. Since functions are restricted to pure classical computation, the type system blocks any call from a function into an operation, including gate calls like H.

questions.q: How does Qiskit/Python handle the equivalent of Q#'s operation/function split?
options: Python enforces an identical compiler-level restriction using `def pure` vs `def quantum`
Python has no such restriction at all — any `def` can mix classical computation and circuit-building or execution calls, relying on programmer discipline rather than the language
Qiskit requires a `@classical_only` decorator enforced at import time
Qiskit circuits cannot call Python functions at all
questions.explain: Qiskit and plain Python have no type-system-level separation between pure helper code and circuit-building/execution code — it's all ordinary functions, and keeping them separate is a matter of convention, not compiler enforcement.

questions.q: In the lesson's `AngleForFraction` / `ApplyFractionalRotation` example, what role does `AngleForFraction` play?
options: It allocates the qubit that `Rz` will act on
It is a pure `function` that computes a classical angle, later consumed by the `operation` as a parameter to `Rz`
It is itself an `operation` because it returns a `Double`
It performs the measurement step of the rotation
questions.explain: AngleForFraction is declared as a function: given the same numerator and denominator it always returns the same Double, with no qubits involved. ApplyFractionalRotation, an operation, calls it and feeds the result into Rz.
